messages.author: ee67d5ba307c0ec7
messages.subject: Using bootstrapLavaan with Modification Indices
parts:
Hello--
I'm hoping to get some help in generating empirical bootstrapped results for modification indices. 

I have fit a CFA model (model below) successfully and been able to calculate target values of the modification indices. I've tried various approaches to pass functions to bootstrapLavaan() but it always returns an empty vector with an error code. For example:

### bootstrap
> bootstrapLavaan(fit.first, R=2
>    , type="ordinary"
>        , FUN=function(x) {c(modificationindices(x,op="=~")$mi)}
>    , parallel="snow", ncpus = parallel::detectCores()
>    , verbose=T)
[,1] ... [,92]
attr(,"error.idx")
[1] 1 2

### model estimation
model.first<-'
      a =~ NA*ItemA1+ItemA2+ItemA3+ItemA4+ItemA5
      c =~ NA*ItemC1+ItemC2+ItemC3+ItemC4
      e =~ NA*ItemE1+ItemE2+ItemE3+ItemE4+ItemE5
      l =~ NA*ItemL1+ItemL2+ItemL3+ItemL4+ItemL5+ItemL6
      r =~ NA*ItemR1+ItemR2+ItemR3
    '
fit.first <- cfa(model.first
  , data=dat.analysis
  , std.lv=T
  , parameterization="delta"
  , orthogonal=F
  , start="Mplus"
  , verbose=T
  , estimator="WLSMV"
  , ordered=colnames(dat.analysis)
)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Using bootstrapLavaan with Modification Indices
parts:
When you use SNOW (available on all platforms) instead of multicore (not available on Windows), you need to make sure any relevant objects are available in the workspace that gets created on the worker nodes. At a minimum, you need to load the lavaan library to use its functions.  Also, in an example using only 2 bootstrap samples, no need to use more than 2 CPUs.

example(cfa)
bootstrapLavaan(fit, R=2, type="ordinary", 
                FUN = function(x) {library(lavaan) ; modificationindices(x,op="=~")$mi},
                parallel="snow", ncpus = 2)
